commits.pr_body:
Add support for MiniCPM-V 4.7, scheduled for release soon.

The architecture is close to 4.6. The main addition is canvas 3D M-RoPE: the
thumbnail is resampled over the slice canvas, and slices and row newlines take
positions from their geometry.

Other changes:
- Video placeholders no longer emit `<image_id>` local ids; 4.7 was trained
  without them.
- 4.6 refactored to be inheritable. Default behavior unchanged.
- Fix canvas `rope_delta` missing `+1`, matching qwen2_vl / qwen3_vl.
- Restore literal `\n` in output. The tokenizer decodes newlines as the two
  chars `\` + `n` (id 1639). Code blocks, inline code, LaTeX and tool call
  arguments are left untouched.

Testing:
- Canvas positions and rope_delta match the transformers 4.7 reference
  (PR #48979) token for token, 7/7 cases.
- 12 tests pass, ruff check and ruff format clean.
- No open PR covers this.

AI assistance was used.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Support scalar priority and wire priority into LLM.chat()
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`OfflineInferenceMixin._add_chat_requests` accepts a priority and applies it:

```python
seq_priority = self._priority_to_seq(priority, len(seq_convs))
```

Its only caller, `_run_chat`, has no `priority` parameter and never passes one, and
neither does `LLM.chat()`. `LLM.generate()`, `LLM.enqueue()` and `LLM.enqueue_chat()`
all expose it, so the value is plumbed the whole way down and is reachable from every
offline entrypoint except this one:

```
>>> llm.chat(messages, priority=1)
TypeError: LLM.chat() got an unexpected keyword argument 'priority'
```

A second defect sits in the same class. `_priority_to_seq` calls `len(priority)`
whenever priority is not `None`, so a single value fails even for a single prompt:

```
>>> llm.generate("Hello", priority=1)
TypeError: object of type 'int' has no len()
```

Its two siblings, `_params_to_seq` and `_lora_request_to_seq`, both test
`isinstance(x, Sequence)` first and broadcast a scalar with `[x] * num_requests`.
`_priority_to_seq` is the only one of the three without that branch.

Normalising `None` to `0` first leaves the rest of its body identical to those two.
Existing callers are unaffected: a list is still length-checked and paired one by one
with the prompts, and `None` still yields `[0] * num_requests`.

The scalar half is the looser of the two, since the annotation did say `list[int]`.
Happy to drop it and keep this to the `LLM.chat()` gap.

### Duplicate-work check

No open PR or issue covers this. Searched open PRs for `priority_to_seq`,
`offline_utils priority` and `offline_utils in:path`, all empty. #50884 also edits
`llm.py` and `offline_utils.py`, for per-prompt seeds, and does not touch priority
handling; I will rebase if it lands first.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_offline_utils.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/llm/test_chat.py -k priority -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/llm/test_generate.py -k priority -v
pre-commit run --files vllm/entrypoints/offline_utils.py vllm/entrypoints/llm.py \
    tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_offline_utils.py \
    tests/entrypoints/llm/test_generate.py tests/entrypoints/llm/test_chat.py
```

`test_scalar_priority_broadcast` extends the existing unit tests and needs no GPU and
no model weights. `test_chat_priority` extends `test_chat.py` and mirrors
`test_multiple_priority` in `test_generate.py`; it needs weights, so it is left to CI.

## Test Result

```
5 passed
```

Reverting `offline_utils.py` fails `test_scalar_priority_broadcast` with
`TypeError: object of type 'int' has no len()` at `offline_utils.py:288`.

pre-commit is clean, including `mypy-3.12` at the manual stage CI uses.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Use the EAGLE replay boundary when retaining sliding-window tails
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`MooncakeStoreCoordinator.store_mask` mirrors the core's sparse sliding-window retention (`SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask`) so the store keeps the same tails the local prefix cache does. It passed the non-EAGLE replay boundary, `(num_prompt_tokens - 1,)`, while masking with `use_eagle=True`. Under EAGLE the lookup matches one block past the hit and drops back from it, so the core's `replay_boundaries` places the boundary one scheduler block lower; the store did not. For a prompt that is not block-aligned the retained tail therefore ended one block too high, the saved prefix held `need - 1` of the `cdiv(sliding_window - 1, block_size) + 1` contiguous blocks the lookup requires, and the joint hit collapsed to 0. Only block-aligned prompts hit.

Affected layout: a full-attention target group plus a sliding-window EAGLE drafter group (DFlash-style, e.g. window 2048 / block 64) with `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`. Same family as #57610 (sparse sliding-window retention keeping a tail exactly `need` blocks long), but on the store side and with a different cause; #57613 composes with this change.

The fix extracts the core rule into a module-level `replay_boundaries()` in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py` (called directly from `KVCacheCoordinator.cache_blocks`, behaviour unchanged) and calls it from `_reachable_masks`, so the two sides cannot drift again. The non-EAGLE path still yields `(num_prompt_tokens - 1,)`. On a block-aligned prompt the store now also keeps the core's lower "resend" tail: one extra sliding-window tail per aligned prompt, identical to what the local cache retains.

Not a duplicate: #56615 pairs Mamba and attention boundaries for partial-tail handoffs and does not touch the retention boundary; #57444 changes the core boundary alignment for fine-grained hits (same function, orthogonal change; trivial rebase whichever lands first); #46906 sidesteps by making store retention dense; #57613 fixes #57610 inside `reachable_block_mask`.

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py`: `test_store_mask_retention_interval_zero_eagle_keeps_lookup_tail` (the mask keeps the `need`-block tail at the lowered boundary, for an unaligned and an aligned prompt) and `test_store_mask_retention_interval_zero_eagle_round_trip` (save through `store_mask`, then the EAGLE lookup hits).
- Existing Mooncake coordinator, worker and scheduler unit tests, and `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` + `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache` for the core refactor.

## Test Result

- Direct-call cleanup validation: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q -k "mooncake or retention or eagle or replay"` — 62 passed, 147 deselected. All pre-commit hooks passed on the three changed files. This cleanup used OpenAI Codex assistance.

- On B300: 677 passed across the suites above. The two `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate` cases error identically on `main` in that environment (the test server cannot fetch its Hub model there) and are unrelated.
- On `main` the new tests fail for the unaligned prompt (mask mismatch; hit 0); with this change they pass.
- Lint: ruff check / format and mypy pass.
- Model output is unaffected: retention only decides which already-computed blocks the store keeps.

AI assistance: this change was developed with Claude (Anthropic) under human direction; every changed line was reviewed by the submitter, who ran the tests above.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Explain disabled scale-out endpoints with opt-in hints
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

After #54579 and #55176, existing callers of `/inference/v1/generate` receive an unexplained 404 unless the server is started with `--enable-scale-out`. This makes a deliberate configuration gate look like a missing or removed API.

Keep the existing opt-in default and dedicated render/tokens-only behavior. Disabled Python scale-out POST routes and Rust `/inference/v1/generate` instead return HTTP 403 with an OpenAI-style error explaining that the server must be restarted with `--enable-scale-out`. The handlers have no request-body parameters and never invoke rendering, generation, or multimodal deserialization. Configured API-key authentication remains in front of them; Python diagnostic routes stay out of OpenAPI. Unknown paths still return 404.

Keep startup diagnostics at INFO in both frontends: an unused optional feature being disabled is normal, not a warning condition. Callers that actually use a disabled endpoint receive the actionable HTTP error. This is not a rollback of the security gate and does not change pickle settings, model execution, or successful generation responses.

The Python diagnostic paths and HTTP methods are derived from the existing routers instead of maintaining a second endpoint list. Error construction reuses the existing `create_error_response` helper; no new global error framework or middleware is introduced.

## Duplicate check

Checked open PRs and issues for scale-out disabled-endpoint errors, `--enable-scale-out`, and 404/403 diagnostics. No existing PR implementing this diagnostic change was found. #56124 concerns Rust render-endpoint support, not this disabled-generation response. This is a follow-up to #54579/#55176, not a duplicate or replacement.

## Validation

- Python: `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/scale_out tests/entrypoints/scale_out/test_factories.py -q`: **24 passed**. Covers all eight disabled Python paths, malformed bodies, authenticated 403 versus unauthenticated 401, hidden OpenAPI entries, unknown-path 404, INFO-only startup logging, and native request validation with explicit opt-in or tokens-only mode.
- Python route/authentication regression: `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints tests/entrypoints/scale_out/test_factories.py tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_authentication_middleware.py -q`: **44 passed** total (includes the 24 above; counts are not additive).
- Ruff check/format, rustfmt check, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks, including mypy, Rust formatting, and commit sign-off: passed.
- Rust: `cargo test -p vllm-server --lib --jobs 2 -- --test-threads=2`: **456 passed**, including disabled-route 403 on a malformed body and tightened enabled-route assertions requiring native HTTP 400 validation rather than merely a non-404 response. Compiled and executed locally in an isolated target directory.
- Broader Python render/Cohere suites could not collect in this environment: CUDA flash-attention extensions and the optional `cohere` SDK are missing. No pass is claimed for those suites, and production code was not altered to bypass these dependencies.
- Model evaluation: not applicable. Only disabled-route diagnostics change; no model output or numerical computation is modified.

## AI assistance

Developed with OpenAI Codex assistance at the human submitter's request. Kept as a draft pending human line-by-line review; human review is not claimed as already completed.

## Overview

Default CORS settings currently allow any website to read responses from a browser-reachable vLLM server. Require operators to opt in to browser origins in both Python and Rust serving frontends.

## Claims

- Default requests from foreign origins receive no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header, and JSON preflight requests are not authorized.
- Explicit `--allowed-origins` settings continue to permit selected browser origins.

## Validation

- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_cors_middleware.py tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_cli_args.py -k cors -q` — 3 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` — relevant hooks passed; overall run failed on an unrelated XPU lockfile drift, existing Linux-only mypy attributes, and a `/private/var` path comparison in the non-root entrypoint test.
- Rust CORS tests: pending Linux run. A local macOS build fails in untouched `engine-core-client` because `socket2::Socket::domain` is unavailable on macOS.

## Details

The default allowed origin list was `["*"]` in both serving implementations. Browser scripts could therefore read API responses from reachable deployments that did not configure an API key. The new default is an empty list, while explicit origin allowlists and wildcard opt-in continue to work. Deployments that intentionally serve browser applications must configure `--allowed-origins` with their trusted origins.

This changes CORS response and preflight behavior. CORS is a browser access control and does not replace API authentication or prevent all simple cross-origin requests from being sent.

## Duplicate-work check

I inspected the diffs of related open PRs #49393, #59892, #58908, and #60988, plus merged PRs #45753 and #52309. None changes the default allowed origins across both serving frontends.

commits.pr_title: [Fast Start][Bugfix] Snapshot GPU memory after external weights are ready
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

When the IPC weight-cache daemon loads zero-copy weights concurrently with engine startup, the current initialization order counts the daemon's late allocations twice. This can leave no valid memory budget for the KV cache even though the GPU has enough free memory.

## Claims

- Take `init_snapshot` after external weight memory is ready.
- Restore automatic KV-cache sizing for static EP IPC loading.

## Validation

```text
python3 -m pytest -q -s tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k qwen3-ep --timeout=1800
```

With a real Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct MoE model used by #57320, TP=2, EP enabled, and the fixed KV-cache override temporarily removed in the validation harness: `1 passed, 15 deselected`. Baseline, cold fallback, warm zero-copy, and zero-copy restart all produced identical outputs; both zero-copy runs mapped 676 tensors per rank. Automatic sizing reported about 28 GiB of available KV-cache memory and 611,440 KV-cache tokens. The test file is unchanged in this PR.

## Details

Assume 100 GiB total memory and `gpu_memory_utilization=90%`:

```text
Memory usage
100 ┤
 90 ┤──────────────────────────────── budget limit
 80 ┤
 75 ┤                         ┌──────────────┐
 70 ┤                         │ daemon 50    │
 60 ┤                         │ engine 25    │
 50 ┤               ┌─────────┴──────────────┘
 40 ┤               │ daemon 50
 30 ┤               │
 20 ┤     ┌─────────┘
 10 ┤     │ daemon 20
  0 ┼─────┴────────────────────────────────────→ time
       t0              t1                 t2
   snapshot        daemon ready       profiling
```

At `t0`, the daemon uses 20 GiB, so `init_snapshot` records 80 GiB free. At `t1`, daemon loading completes at 50 GiB and `get_memory()` reports 50 GiB. At `t2`, the engine itself uses 25 GiB, so the actual total is 75 GiB.

The target budget is 90 GiB. The intended engine budget is `90 - 50 = 40 GiB`, but profiling measures `80 - 25 = 55 GiB` from the old snapshot. That 55 GiB includes the daemon's late 30 GiB allocation and the engine's 25 GiB allocation. The daemon's 30 GiB is therefore charged once through `get_memory()` and again through the profiling delta. The resulting requested KV-cache budget is reduced by 30 GiB too much; in the real Qwen3 EP test it became `-2.46 GiB`, so KV-cache initialization failed.

With the snapshot taken after daemon readiness, the profiling delta is `50 - 25 = 25 GiB`, which measures only engine allocations. The external-weight deduction and profiling baseline then describe the same memory state.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Reclaim cached GPU memory during weight loading
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57440.

During `BaseModelLoader.load_model()`, temporary tensors created in `load_weights()` and `process_weights_after_loading()` (such as FP8/MXFP4 weight repacking buffers) remain reserved in PyTorch's caching allocator pool (`reserved - allocated`). On discrete GPUs, `release_device_memory_under_pressure()` is a no-op because it only runs on integrated GPUs, leaving raw CUDA driver allocations (such as DeepEP v2 `cuMemCreate` / DMA-BUF buffers, `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1`, or secondary model fit checks via `mem_get_info()`) starved of free driver HBM.

This PR adds `gc.collect()` and `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` (when `current_platform.is_cuda_alike()`) at the two weight-loading lifecycle boundaries in `BaseModelLoader.load_model()`:
1. Immediately after `self.load_weights(model, model_config)` before `process_weights_after_loading()`
2. Immediately after `process_weights_after_loading(model, model_config, target_device)`

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_base_loader_memory.py -q
```

## Test Result

`2 passed` verifying the exact ordering of `load_weights` -> `gc.collect` / `empty_cache` -> `process_weights_after_loading` -> `gc.collect` / `empty_cache` on CUDA-alike platforms and skipping `empty_cache` on non-CUDA platforms.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Preserve each Qwen3-VL video's effective sampling options across repeated items and partial multimodal-cache hits. Reject option lists that are too short before indexing them.

## Claims

- Each video's selected `fps` and `num_frames` contribute to its cache identity.
- Partial cache hits filter option lists together with the remaining videos.
- Configured defaults, request options, flat/nested scopes, UUID reuse, and encoder profiling preserve their existing behavior.
- Short option lists raise a clear `ValueError` with and without a processor cache. Unused trailing entries remain supported.

## Validation

Validated on 2026-10-11 at head `a0067713d3`, rebased onto upstream `01abe975b5`.

```sh
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' uv run --no-project -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_vl.py -q
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' uv run --no-project -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_cache.py tests/multimodal/test_processing.py -q
uv run --no-project -- .venv/bin/pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_vl.py
```

The Qwen3 processor, generic processing, and cache suites pass, as do the applicable scoped hooks. The CUDA sleep/wake integration was skipped in the CPU suite. The short-list reproducer failed with `IndexError: list index out of range` before the guard and raises the expected `ValueError` afterward. Regressions exercise empty/short lists, warm caches, longer lists through partial hits, and profiling with fewer videos than configured options.

The cache regression checks prompts, placeholders, tensors, hashes, scalar-reference grids, duplicate videos, partial hits, reordering, model/request options, flat/nested scopes, and UUID-only reuse. Input options remain unmodified.

| Loaded-model comparison | Configuration/result |
| --- | --- |
| Model/runtime | Real `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct` weights, snapshot `89644892e4d85e24eaac8bacfd4f463576704203`; RTX 5070 Ti, BF16, MRV2, FlashAttention 2, eager execution |
| Workload | Synthetic video pairs with `num_frames=[8,16]`, duplicate/partial/reordered cache use against uncached references; greedy 8-token generation |
| Result | Prompt IDs, placeholders, tensors, hashes, output token IDs, and complete top-5 logprob maps match; maximum logprob difference **0.0** |

Validation used the shared development environment, pinned Humming 0.1.16, and existing precompiled CUDA extensions. Optional FlashInfer autotuning and JIT warmup were disabled. This is a focused 2B family comparison, not a 4B answer-quality benchmark.

## Details

Request-wide option-list hashes let repeated videos reuse the first video's result despite different sampling settings. Partial hits removed videos without removing the corresponding option entries.

The existing base hooks let Qwen3-VL refine item hashes and select cache-miss options while preserving other processors. The final text/image HF call suppresses configured video lists so merging cannot reintroduce them. The review fix stays in the Qwen3 processor and its existing regression suite.

Merged #56372 handles option scoping and the cache API; this fix uses that behavior. The current overlap search found no competing per-item cache identity/partial-hit fix. #54527 addresses scoped option reads in other models; #60879 bounds MiniMax video decoding.

Affected hashes retain the full option list as well as selected item options, so equivalent reordered requests can incur extra misses. Scalar paths retain their existing hashes.

[Upstream pre-commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/38111515737/job/114387896372) is blocked at contributor authorization before implementation checks run. [Read the Docs](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35068511/) reports success from skipping this change because no docs-affecting files changed; MkDocs did not run. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, validation, and review.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] MSA prefill attends with the E4M3 query; bump fmha_sm100 to 968061a
commits.pr_body:
## Overview With CUTLASS MSA sparse decode on (an NVFP4 KV cache, or an FP8 E4M3 cache with the `CUTLASS_MSA` decode backend), the fused QK-norm/RoPE/insert kernel writes MiniMax-M3's query only in E4M3. `MiniMaxM3SparseMSAImpl` then dequantized it back into the BF16 query buffer before every prefill. Both `fmha_sm100` prefill kernels take an E4M3 query natively, so prefill now passes it through as is. The PR also bumps `fmha_sm100` (vllm-project/MSA) from `be4a52a` to `968061a`. The new pin includes MSA's Blackwell prefill port, which now serves an E4M3 query over vLLM's packed K|V pages (vllm-project/MSA#32). ## Claims - MSA prefill attention is **26–37% faster with an FP8 KV cache** and **8–13% faster with an NVFP4 KV cache** than on main (per layer on GB300; table below). - Prefill no longer makes a BF16 copy of the query. Only the Triton decode fallback still reads the dequantized query. - BF16 caches and the default Triton decode backend for FP8 caches still pass a BF16 query, so their path is unchanged. ## Validation **Tests:** on GB300 (SM103, CUDA 13.4, `fmha_sm100` built from the new pin), `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_fp8_triton_indexer.py tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py tests/kernels/test_minimax_m3_sparse_attn_fp8_scale.py tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py` gives **240 passed, 45 skipped**. All skips are ROCm-only tests. The MSA test file runs in CI on B200. - New `test_msa_prefill_reads_query_fp8_over_fp8_cache[tp1|tp4]` covers FP8-cache prefill, including chunks over cached context, with CUTLASS decode on. It checks that `sparse_atten_func` receives the E4M3 query and that the output matches Triton on the dequantized query. - `test_msa_prefill_nvfp4_matches_triton_on_dequantized_cache` now checks that `sparse_atten_nvfp4_kv_func` receives the E4M3 query. Its reference is now the cache as an E4M3-query kernel reads it (see Details). - Both prefill tests require all but 1e-4 of the elements within atol/rtol 0.05 and bound the rest at 0.25. The E4M3 probabilities are rounded per split, and splits follow the SM count, so a rare element lands just past 0.05: 1 of 4.1M on B200 CI. On GB300 over 16 seeds the worst case is 2.4e-7 of the elements and 0.07 max abs error. - On the old code, all four prefill cases fail with `[torch.bfloat16] == [torch.float8_e4m3fn]`. **Performance:** `MiniMaxM3SparseMSAImpl.forward` on prefill-only batches (`build_k2q_csr` + attention + combine, plus the dequant where the query is BF16). GB300, one request, top-k 16, page 128. Each value is the median of 3×50 iterations after warmup; spread ≤1%, except ±5% on the first FP8 row of the main run. | KV cache | Q heads / KV heads | Query tokens @ cached context | main (MSA `be4a52a`, BF16 q) | pin bump only (BF16 q) | this PR (E4M3 q) | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | FP8 | 16 / 1 (TP4) | 8k @ 0 | 411 µs | 368 µs | 303 µs (-26%) | | FP8 | 16 / 1 | 8k @ 32k | 462 µs | 439 µs | 314 µs (-32%) | | FP8 | 16 / 1 | 16k @ 112k | 801 µs | 754 µs | 530 µs (-34%) | | FP8 | 64 / 4 (TP1) | 8k @ 0 | 1423 µs | 1320 µs | 891 µs (-37%) | | FP8 | 64 / 4 | 8k @ 32k | 1498 µs | 1423 µs | 985 µs (-34%) | | NVFP4 | 16 / 1 | 8k @ 0 | 379 µs | 375 µs | 342 µs (-10%) | | NVFP4 | 16 / 1 | 8k @ 32k | 457 µs | 458 µs | 420 µs (-8%) | | NVFP4 | 16 / 1 | 16k @ 112k | 798 µs | 795 µs | 695 µs (-13%) | | NVFP4 | 64 / 4 | 8k @ 0 | 1411 µs | 1395 µs | 1255 µs (-11%) | | NVFP4 | 64 / 4 | 8k @ 32k | 1491 µs | 1491 µs | 1317 µs (-12%) | Percentages are relative to main. With the new pin, a BF16 query over the FP8 cache also reaches the Blackwell port, but with BF16 MMAs. The E4M3 query gives the bulk of the FP8 gain at either pin: on main's pin alone it is 13–24% (411 → 356, 462 → 367, 801 → 623, 1423 → 1083, 1498 → 1162 µs).
Benchmark script (run from the repo root with PYTHONPATH=.) ```python """Per-layer MSA prefill attention (impl.forward) with an E4M3 query.""" import math from types import SimpleNamespace import torch import tests.kernels.attention.test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode as t from vllm.forward_context import ForwardContext, override_forward_context from vllm.models.minimax_m3.common.sparse_attention import ( MiniMaxM3SparseMetadata, MiniMaxM3SparsePrefillMetadata) BLK, TOPK = 128, 16 def case(q_len, seq_len, hkv, g): pos = torch.arange(seq_len - q_len, seq_len, device="cuda") visible = pos // BLK + 1 vmax = int(visible.max()) r = torch.rand(q_len, hkv, vmax, device="cuda", generator=g) ar = torch.arange(vmax, device="cuda") r = torch.where(ar < visible[:, None, None] - 1, r, -1.0) r = torch.where(ar == visible[:, None, None] - 1, 2.0, r) k = min(TOPK, vmax) val, idx = r.topk(k, dim=-1) topk = torch.where(val >= 0, idx, -1).int() if k < TOPK: topk = torch.cat([topk, topk.new_full((q_len, hkv, TOPK - k), -1)], -1) pages = math.ceil(seq_len / BLK) block_table = torch.randperm(pages, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")[None] seq = torch.tensor([seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") cu_q = torch.tensor([0, q_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") cu_k = torch.tensor([0, seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") p = MiniMaxM3SparsePrefillMetadata( cu_seqlens_q=cu_q, cu_seqlens_k=cu_k, seq_lens=seq, context_lens=seq - q_len, block_table=block_table, max_query_len=q_len, max_seq_len=seq_len, total_kv_blocks=pages) md = MiniMaxM3SparseMetadata( seq_lens=seq, max_seq_len=seq_len, slot_mapping=torch.empty(q_len, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda"), num_actual_tokens=q_len, num_decodes=0, num_decode_tokens=0, num_prefills=1, num_prefill_tokens=q_len, prefill=p) return md, topk, pages def bench(fn, iters=50): for _ in range(10): fn() torch.cuda.synchronize() s, e = torch.cuda.Event(True), torch.cuda.Event(True) s.record() for _ in range(iters): fn() e.record() torch.cuda.synchronize() return s.elapsed_time(e) / iters * 1e3 g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0) for kv_dtype in ("fp8", "nvfp4"): for hq, hkv, q_len, ctx in ((16, 1, 8192, 0), (16, 1, 8192, 32768), (16, 1, 16384, 114688), (64, 4, 8192, 0), (64, 4, 8192, 32768)): md, topk, pages = case(q_len, ctx + q_len, hkv, g) k_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, device="cuda") v_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, device="cuda") if kv_dtype == "nvfp4": kv_cache, _ = t._make_nvfp4_kv_cache(pages, hkv, "nvfp4", k_scale, v_scale) else: kv_cache = (torch.randn(pages, hkv, BLK, 256, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) layer = SimpleNamespace(layer_name="l", topk_indices_buffer=topk, _q_scale_float=0.5, _k_scale=k_scale, _v_scale=v_scale) qf = torch.randn(q_len, hq * 128, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) query = torch.empty(q_len, hq * 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") out = torch.empty_like(query) impl = t.MiniMaxM3SparseMSAImpl( num_heads=hq, head_size=128, scale=t.SM_SCALE, num_kv_heads=hkv, kv_cache_dtype=kv_dtype, topk_blocks=TOPK, sparse_block_size=BLK, msa_decode_backend="cutlass") assert impl.use_cutlass_decode with override_forward_context(ForwardContext(no_compile_layers={}, attn_metadata={"l": md}, slot_mapping={})): bench(lambda: impl.forward(layer, query, kv_cache, out, query_fp8=qf), iters=200) ts = [bench(lambda: impl.forward(layer, query, kv_cache, out, query_fp8=qf)) for _ in range(3)] print(f"{kv_dtype} H{hq}/{hkv} q{q_len} ctx{ctx}: " + " ".join(f"{x:.1f}" for x in ts) + " us") ```
**No end-to-end accuracy eval or serving benchmark** is included; validation is the kernel-level numerics and per-layer timings above. ## Details **Kernel capability (MSA `968061a`; same at `be4a52a` except the Blackwell port):** - `sparse_atten_func` accepts an FP8 E4M3 query over FP8 E4M3 K/V and runs FP8 QK/PV MMAs, on the Blackwell port when eligible. The BF16-Q × FP8-K/V mode stages K/V up to BF16 instead. - `sparse_atten_nvfp4_kv_func` accepts a BF16 or E4M3 query. With E4M3 it dequantizes each NVFP4 `code × block_scale` to E4M3 instead of BF16, and applies the K global scale to the scores and the V global scale in the combine. **Scales:** `q_scale` folds into `softmax_scale`. The FP8 cache is written with unit scales and the NVFP4 global scales are passed as before, so K/V scale handling is unchanged. **Numerics:** the E4M3-query kernels round the softmax probabilities to E4M3. The NVFP4 kernel also rounds K/V to E4M3. On the NVFP4 test (TP1): - Against the E4M3-staged cache: max abs error 0.06, and 0 of 4.1M elements outside atol/rtol 0.05. - Against the exact BF16 dequantization: max 0.14, with 122 of 4.1M elements outside that tolerance. This is why the test's reference changed. On the FP8 test the max abs error is ≈0.03. **Limitations:** validated on SM103. SM100 is covered by the CI kernel job. The E4M3-query NVFP4 kernel is untested on SM107 here. **MSA pin bump (`be4a52a` → `968061a`):** - The functions vLLM calls keep their signatures: `fmha_sm100`, `fmha_sm100_plan`, `_fmha_sm100(_plan)`, `sparse_topk_select`, `sparse_atten_func`, `sparse_atten_nvfp4_kv_func` and `nvfp4_head_slot_views`. - vLLM's decode plans still pin `decode_backend="kv_mode3"`. The new `prefill_backend` plan option only routes sparse-prefill plans built through `fmha_sm100_plan`, which vLLM does not use. - The cmake install list adds the files the package now imports: `_jit_cache.py`, `msa_warmup.py`, `q8kv4_prefill_adapter.py` and `prefill_q8kv4/`. **Duplicate check:** no open PR touches the MSA prefill query or `fmha_sm100.cmake`. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix speculative block reservations across KV cache groups
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix speculative decode block reservations for asynchronous KV loads with
multiple KV cache groups. Under KV memory pressure, under-reserving these
blocks can leave a request admitted for an asynchronous KV load but unable
to start decoding once the load completes.

## Claims

- Account for every KV cache group using its actual allocation block size.
- Extend the existing promotion-margin regression test to cover single-group,
  multi-group, and mixed-block-size configurations.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py
```

**32 passed.** Pre-commit checks and manual Python 3.12 mypy passed.

Regression controls replace only the reservation method in the test process:

| Implementation | Single group | Multiple groups | Different block sizes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Original | Pass | Fail | Fail |
| Original × group count | Pass | Pass | Fail |
| This fix | Pass | Pass | Pass |

The broader scheduler/decode/recovery run showed no additional failures:
both the patched implementation and the original reservation method produced
171 passes and the same 46 failing test IDs. Observed environment limitations
included unavailable offline model configurations and insufficient visible
GPUs for parallel tests.

Validation exercises the scheduler and KV allocation paths with simulated
remote completion. Live NIXL P/D and model-level evaluations were not run.

## Details

The existing calculation converts the speculative token margin to blocks
using the scheduler block size once. However, each KV cache group allocates
independently from the shared block pool, and groups may use different
allocation block sizes.

Sum the reservation across cache managers using each manager's block size.
Simply multiplying the old result by the group count is insufficient for
mixed-block-size configurations. The existing conservative reservation
approach is preserved.

The regression test checks admission and subsequent scheduling rather than
asserting the helper's arithmetic directly.

---

commits.pr_title: [RL][Frontend] Return token-level weight-version spans on final outputs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

**Draft for early testing.** This is a first version for others to try; it will change.

RL rollouts often cross a weight update. With `pause(mode="keep")`, a running request is frozen, the weights and the weight-version label change, and the request resumes, so one output is sampled by two weight versions. vLLM only reports the engine's current label (`/weight_info`), so the caller cannot tell which tokens came from which weights.

This PR returns, on the final output of every sequence, the label of the weights that sampled each range of output tokens:

```json
"weight_versions": [
  {"version": "v7", "start": 0,  "end": 57},
  {"version": "v8", "start": 57, "end": 128}
]
```

Behavior:
- **Shape.** There is one list per output sequence, made of half-open ranges over output-token indexes (prompt excluded). The ranges are contiguous and in generation order, and they cover every returned token once.
- **Labels.** Adjacent ranges with the same label merge; A → B → A gives three ranges. An output with no tokens gets `[]`.
- **Capture point.** A token's label is the engine's label when the step that sampled it returns its outputs. The update flow sets the label while generation is paused, when no step is in flight, so every token gets the label of the weights that sampled it.
- **Delivery.** The list is returned only on the final output, including aborted outputs. A stream sends it on its last chunk, and that chunk is still sent when it has no new tokens (e.g. an abort).
- **Surfaces.** The list is exposed as `CompletionOutput.weight_versions` and on `/inference/v1/generate` choices in both output modes (non-stream and the final stream chunk). OpenAI-compatible endpoints are unchanged in this PR.

Implementation:
- `EngineCore` stamps its current label on each step's `EngineCoreOutputs`, next to the existing iteration details. The scheduler and the weight-update path are unchanged.
- `OutputProcessor` records a span start whenever a request's tokens arrive under a different label than its previous ones, and builds the spans on the final output.
- `RequestOutput.add` takes the spans from the last merged output, like `finish_reason`. Merged DELTA outputs therefore keep them, and output merged past the end of a streaming-input chunk does not carry stale ones.
- The Rust engine-core client decodes the new `EngineCoreOutputs` field, because it rejects unknown trailing fields of that struct. It does not expose the field yet.
- Docs: the token-in/token-out and async RL pages describe the field and where to set the label. The async RL example now reads the swap point from `weight_versions` instead of pausing, sleeping five seconds and counting streamed tokens. CI runs that example, so its check against a fresh instance of the new model now also covers the span boundary.

Not a duplicate:
- Another open draft reports one weight version per output: each streamed chunk carries the label current when it was formed, and a non-streaming response carries the label of its last output.
- That cannot say which tokens of a non-streaming response came from which weights, and a streamed chunk that merges outputs from both sides of an update carries one label.
- This PR returns the ranges themselves, per completion. Token-level masking and per-segment replay of `routed_experts` or `sampling_mask` need these offsets.

This change only adds metadata. It does not change scheduling, sampling or the generated tokens, so no model evaluation is included.

## Test Plan

Unit tests (CPU):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -k weight_version
cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client
```

End-to-end on H20, on this revision: the precompiled wheel of the base commit with this PR's Python files on top.
- **`/inference/v1/generate`.** Two servers with Qwen3-1.7B, `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1` and `--enable-scale-out`, one with async scheduling and one without.
  - **Weight update.** A worker extension zeroes `lm_head` through `/collective_rpc`, and `/update_weight_version` sets a new label. After that, greedy decoding emits only token 0, so each span boundary must sit at the first 0 token.
  - **Scenarios, in both output modes (`tokens` and `text`):**
    - `pause(mode="keep")` with `clear_cache=false` and with `clear_cache=true`, using three streams and one non-streaming request, plus a request admitted during the pause;
    - `pause(mode="abort")` with streams, a non-streaming request and a long-prompt request sent just before the abort;
    - a request after resume, and `/weight_info`.
- **Example.** `examples/rl/rlhf_async_new_apis.py` on two GPUs, with only the model names pointed at local copies of the same checkpoints:

```bash
VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1 python examples/rl/rlhf_async_new_apis.py
```

## Test Result

- **Unit tests:** the new test passes in all 4 parametrizations, and `vllm-engine-core-client` passes 125/125.
- **Existing tests in the touched areas** (the output processor, scheduler and outputs tests, and all `/inference/v1/generate` tests): they give the same results as on the base commit, including the same 59 errors on both, which come from the CPU test environment (e.g. model weights not available offline).
- **End-to-end, `/inference/v1/generate`:** 135/135 checks pass with async scheduling on, and 135/135 with it off.
  - **keep:** streams and non-streaming requests got `[("A", 0, k), ("B", k, 300)]` with k between 17 and 21. Every token from k on was 0, and the token before k was not. Requests admitted during the pause got `[("B", 0, 64)]`.
  - **abort:** every aborted request ended with `finish_reason: "abort"` and one span over its partial output, including final chunks with no new tokens. The long-prompt request was aborted before its first token once (async scheduling on, `tokens` mode) and got `[]`. In the other three runs it had already produced one token and got one span.
  - **after resume:** one span with the unchanged label, and `/weight_info` returned the last label.
- **Example:** passes, with 13/13 prompts matching a fresh instance of the new model. The swap points read from `weight_versions` were 10 tokens for 12 prompts and 12 tokens for one.

Coverage notes:
- The unit test covers the span logic in `OutputProcessor`. `EngineCore` stamping the label and the `/inference/v1/generate` changes are covered by the end-to-end runs and the example.
- The streaming-input chunk-end case of `RequestOutput.add` is not tested.

On current main, `/inference/v1/generate` is only registered with `--enable-scale-out` (or `--tokens-only`).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the code, the tests and this description.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Support 0-dim tensors in packed weight transfer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Packed weight transfer currently fails for 0-D (scalar) tensors.

On the producer side, `pack_tensors` and `packed_ipc_producer` reinterpret each tensor as `uint8` before flattening it. Reinterpreting to a dtype with a different element size requires `dim() > 0`, so a scalar raises:

```text
RuntimeError: self.dim() cannot be 0 to view Float as Byte (different element sizes)
```

On the consumer side, `unpack_tensor` restores the original shape with `.view(*shape)`. For a scalar, `shape == []`, so the call becomes `view()` and raises `TypeError`.

A single scalar fails the entire chunk it is packed into, not just that tensor.

The unpacked IPC path does not have either problem: it ships tensors through `reduce_tensor`/`rebuild_cuda_tensor` with no dtype reinterpretation, so it round-trips 0-D tensors already. Packed mode is documented as a bounded-memory alternative to the same transfer, so both should accept the same inputs. The receiving side is also prepared for shape-less weights: `weight_loader` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py` reshapes them on load, noting that scales "often do not have a shape (such as in the case of AutoFP8)". `unpack_tensor` raises before that handling runs.

## Changes

Both packed producer paths now flatten before reinterpreting the dtype, so the `uint8` view never sees a 0-dim tensor. `unpack_tensor` passes the shape sequence to `view()` rather than unpacking it, which is valid when the shape is empty.

`view(shape)` is used rather than `reshape(shape)` to preserve `unpack_tensor`'s existing view semantics. Both changes are byte-identical for every shape the existing tests cover, including the transposed, strided and permuted cases.

The flatten-before-reinterpret order matches what the rest of the codebase already does, including `shm_broadcast.py` in this same package:

* `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py`: `.contiguous().reshape(-1).view(torch.uint8)`
* `vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/cpu/worker/__init__.py`: `.view(-1).view(torch.uint8)`
* `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/b12x.py`: `workspace.view(-1).view(torch.uint8)`
* `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/nvfp4/fbgemm.py`: `.view(-1).view(torch.uint8)` (two sites)

Test coverage:

* One parameterized CPU `test_pack_unpack_scalar` covering scalar + matrix over `float32`, `float16`, and `bfloat16`; verifies names, shapes, dtypes, exact values, and equal result lengths. It exercises both pack and unpack, replacing the redundant standalone unpack test.
* a scalar added to the existing `test_roundtrip_basic`, so the fix is exercised through `packed_ipc_producer` as well

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py
```

`pack_tensors` and `unpack_tensor` are device-agnostic, so the new test needs no CUDA guard. The IPC round-trip test remains CUDA-only.

`pre-commit run --files` on both changed files passes locally: ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy-3.10, SPDX headers and the forbidden-import checks.

## Test Result

Latest test-only simplification (`1f67153`):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py -k scalar -q
# 3 passed, 26 deselected
ruff check tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py
ruff format --check tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py
# Both pass
```

The full CUDA/IPC suite was not rerun in this follow-up. The scalar added to the existing CUDA IPC round-trip remains unchanged. The original author reported the pre-simplification CPU reproducer as 4 failures before the source fix, and 4 passes after it, with 26 CUDA tests skipped.

AI assistance was used for the test simplification; the three-line source fix is unchanged.

## Purpose

Fixes #60971. `--enable-log-outputs` (and `--enable-log-deltas`) were accepted as server-wide flags but never forwarded to the Anthropic `/v1/messages` handler, so output logging stayed at its parent defaults there even though `create_messages` reuses the shared `create_chat_completion` implementation where the logging is gated on `self.enable_log_outputs`.

Two changes:

- `AnthropicServingMessages.__init__` now accepts `enable_log_outputs` / `enable_log_deltas` (defaults matching the parent: `False` / `True`) and forwards both to `OpenAIServingChat.__init__`.
- `init_generate_state` passes `args.enable_log_outputs` / `args.enable_log_deltas` when constructing the handler, same as the adjacent Chat Completions setup.

## Why this is not duplicating existing work

The issue (filed today) has no linked PR. Searched open PRs for `60971` and for `enable_log_outputs anthropic`; nothing open or merged touches the Anthropic handler's flag wiring.

## Test plan

Tests removed per maintainer review; the change is constructor-level flag forwarding only, covered by CI.

## AI assistance disclosure

Prepared with AI assistance (Kimi K3). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.
